Since 2020 they have shared Tithe Farm with Rayners Lane, and in 2022-23 they moved into the Combined Counties League Premier Division North.

opponents.historySummary: Harefield United trace their roots to 1868, which makes them the oldest club in Middlesex, and they played under several names before a 1934 merger produced the current one. They won titles in the Great Western Combination, the Parthenon League and the Middlesex League, then had a decade in the Isthmian League. Back in the Spartan South Midlands League, they won Division One unbeaten in 2018-19. They moved across to the Combined Counties League in 2022.

Took the name Harefield United after a 1934 merger with Harefield FC.
Great Western Combination champions in 1950-51 and Parthenon League champions in 1964-65.
Played in the Isthmian League from the mid-1980s until 1996.
Won Spartan South Midlands Division One unbeaten in 2018-19 and joined the Combined Counties Premier North in 2022.

opponents.historySummary: Northwood are generally dated to 1926, although a club existed in the area earlier. They won the Harrow & Wembley League several times either side of the Second World War. After winning the Middlesex League in 1978 they climbed through the Hellenic and Spartan leagues, winning the Spartan title in 1991-92 to join the Isthmian League. Their best era came in the early 2000s, when they reached the Isthmian Premier Division. They have played at Northwood Park on Chestnut Avenue for many years.
historyFacts: Believed to have been formed in 1926 (an earlier Northwood club existed from 1899); joined the Harrow & Wembley League in 1931.
Won the Middlesex League in 1978 and the Hellenic League Division One in their first season after that.
Spartan League Premier Division champions in 1991-92, then admitted to the Isthmian League.
Won Isthmian Division One North in 2002-03, reaching step three for the first time.
Won the Middlesex Senior Cup in 2006-07, beating Hayes on penalties.

They helped found the Hellenic League in 1953 and were its Premier Division champions a decade later. Long spells in the Spartan and Spartan South Midlands leagues followed, including some lean seasons in the lower divisions. A switch to the Combined Counties League in 2023 brought immediate success, with the Division One title earning promotion.

Founder members of the Hellenic League in 1953 and winners of its first League Cup in 1953-54.
Hellenic League Premier Division champions in 1963-64.
Moved to Spratleys Meadow in 1920; its stand was destroyed in the Great Storm of 1987.
Won Combined Counties League Division One in 2023-24 with 111 points.

opponents.historySummary: New Bradwell St Peter began as a church side in Milton Keynes in the 1890s and took their present name after a merger in 1946. They won the North Bucks & District League three times before stepping up to the South Midlands League in 1970, where they twice won Division One. They were the first Senior Division champions of the merged Spartan South Midlands League in 1997-98. The present club took on the historic name in 2018.
historyFacts: Established by 1895 as Stantonbury St James by the Rev. Edmund Marshall; took the current name after a 1946 merger with New Bradwell Corinthians.
North Bucks & District League champions in 1912-13, 1913-14 and 1938-39.
South Midlands League Division One champions in 1976-77 and 1983-84.
Spartan South Midlands Senior Division champions in 1997-98 and Berks & Bucks Senior Trophy winners in 1999-2000.
The original club resigned in 2017; in 2018 Loughton Manor adopted the New Bradwell St Peter name and moved to the Recreation Ground.

opponents.historySummary: Penn & Tylers Green, from near Beaconsfield, adopted their first formal constitution in 1905 and spent decades collecting Wycombe league titles. They bought French School Meadow in 1949; the ground's name and the club's blue and white colours both come from an old school for French orphans. They helped found the Chiltonian League in 1984 and joined the Hellenic League in 2000. They won Combined Counties Division One in 2025-26 to reach this division.
historyFacts: Formally established in 1905; first won the Wycombe League in 1911-12.
Bought French School Meadow in 1949.
Founder members of the Chiltonian League in 1984.
Hellenic Division One East champions in 2015-16 and 2016-17, and runners-up in 2002-03.
Combined Counties League Division One champions in 2025-26; record crowd of 1,237 against Wycombe Wanderers in October 2025.
